topic: Animals of Australia, Africa and South America

payload.title: Animals of Australia, Africa and South America

explanations.Koala: A tree-dwelling marsupial, and so a mammal, native to eastern and southern Australia.
explanations.Giraffe: A hoofed African mammal, the tallest land animal, ranging from Chad to South Africa.
explanations.Llama: A domesticated South American camelid, a mammal of the Andes.
explanations.Emu: A tall flightless bird found across the Australian mainland, and Australia's national bird.
explanations.Ostrich: A large flightless bird found in the wild only in Africa.
explanations.Andean condor: A vulture of the Andes, the largest bird of prey in South America.
explanations.Thorny devil: A spiny lizard, and so a reptile, of the arid scrubland of central Australia.
explanations.Nile crocodile: A large crocodilian, and so a reptile, native to fresh water across Africa.
explanations.Green anaconda: A boa, and so a reptile, found in the rivers and wetlands of South America.

sources.excerpt: The koala (Phascolarctos cinereus), sometimes inaccurately called the koala bear, is an arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia.
Giraffes (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Lama is a genus containing the South American camelids: the wild guanaco and vicuña and the domesticated llama, alpaca, and extinct chilihueque.
The emu is popularly but unofficially considered as a faunal emblem – the national bird of Australia.

Today, ostriches are only found naturally in the wild in Africa, where they occur in a range of open arid and semi-arid habitats such as savannas and the Sahel, both north and south of the equatorial forest zone.
The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
The thorny devil usually lives in the arid scrubland and desert that covers most of central Australia, sandplain and sandridge desert in the deep interior and the mallee belt.
The Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) is a large crocodilian native to freshwater habitats in Africa, where it is present in 26 countries.
The green anaconda (Eunectes murinus), common anaconda, common water boa, akayima, or sucuri, is a boa species found in South America.

editorNotes: Every tile here belongs to exactly one class and one continent, so each fits a single cell. The pairs that look interchangeable are the ones to check. The emu and the ostrich are both large flightless birds, but the emu is endemic to Australia and the ostrich is found in the wild only in Africa, so neither can take the other's cell. The koala is a marsupial and the llama a camelid, and both are mammals, but the koala is native to Australia alone and the llama to South America alone. The Nile crocodile and the green anaconda are both reptiles of warm fresh water, yet the crocodile's range is African and the anaconda's South American; the thorny devil, the third reptile, is an Australian desert lizard. The Andean condor is a bird of the Andes and adjacent Pacific coasts only, so it cannot stand in for the African or Australian bird. With every tile fitting one cell, the placement is forced and unique.
